summary: Snapshot 2026-10-31, all inside the GLP-1 focus. No news item qualifies for Lane C today. The biggest fresh story is retatrutide's TRANSCEND-T2D-2 result, now 3+ days old, so it belongs in Shorts only. The ATTAIN-J orforglipron paper came out Oct 30, but its topline was public earlier, and this year Japan-only trials have drawn little search interest, so it also goes to a Short. That makes 11-01 a Lane A day. Ranked opportunities: (1) stopping tirzepatide, the next queued Lane A, refreshed by the Oct 29 Diabetes Obes Metab persistence cohort and the Metabolites regain review; (2) hair loss, also queued; (3) a new seasonal hook: colds, flu and sick days on tirzepatide (Yahoo Health, Oct 31). Cold and flu season is starting, and nobody in our niche has covered it except telehealth SEO blogs. (4) Thanksgiving on tirzepatide is accelerating across 8 snapshots. Thanksgiving is Nov 26, so publish before the search peak in the week of Nov 16–25. Next come the fatigue/hydration and fibre/constipation Lane A slots. Then body-worry Shorts, our best Short format: older adults and frailty (JAMA, Oct 30, plus the SELECT frailty post hoc), mood and panic-attack worries (a notoriety-bias pharmacovigilance paper), and kidney stones and hydration. Rejected: the Forbes 'where to buy' affiliate list, the Page Six '$99' promo, 'retatrutide cost per mg for research buyers', the peptide liver-failure story (a gray-market hook) and the 'GLP-1 cures cancer' hype. Fact-checker flags: the tirzepatide fatigue rates I found (about 5–7% vs 3% on placebo in SURMOUNT-1) came from secondary sites, so verify them against the current Zepbound label (revised 28 Aug 2026). The cold-medicine angle must stay general ('ask your pharmacist'), with no product or dosing advice.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (783 began the lead-in; 335 vs 335 randomized at week 36; +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88 on placebo), refreshed by the Oct 29 Diabetes Obes Metab population cohort on early treatment trajectory and long-term persistence, and the Metabolites systematic review of regain (Oct 9)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 'Tirzepatide: What Happens When You Stop?' Open on 'You're thinking about stopping tirzepatide. Here's what the biggest trial saw.' Answer in sentence one: in SURMOUNT-4, people switched to placebo regained part of the weight; those who stayed on it kept losing. Then cover what the regain review shows across drugs, why appetite returns (the GLP-1 hormone explained), and the habits that were linked to slower regain (protein, strength training). Say 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own' word for word. Put it in the 'Life on Tirzepatide' playlist.
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
do you gain weight back after tirzepatide

candidates.why_now: Seen in 8 snapshots at a steady 80–84. New Oct 29 persistence cohort. Bloomberg (Oct 30) and Medical Daily report employer coverage shrinking during open enrollment, so many people will be forced to stop and will search what happens. Next in the Lane A queue.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common is it and what helps? 5.4% (119/2,183) vs 0.9% (22/2,221) (Gupta 2026); the label reports 7.1% of women vs 0.5% of men; refreshed by the Med Sci (Basel) cutaneous adverse events systematic review (Oct 9)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 'Tirzepatide Hair Loss: How Common Is It?' The first sentence gives the number. Then: it's particularly associated with rapid weight loss, why shedding often happens months later (telogen effluvium explained simply), why protein and overall nutrition matter, and when to talk to a prescriber or dermatologist. Never say 'it isn't the drug'. Say 'no human studies show a direct effect on follicles'. Calm, encouraging tone.

candidates.topic: Cold and flu season on tirzepatide: sick days, staying hydrated when you can't eat, and why to check with a pharmacist before taking a cold remedy (Yahoo Health, Oct 31)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form or a body-worry Short: 'Tirzepatide and a Cold or Flu: What to Know'. General, label-based points: vomiting or diarrhoea plus low intake can dehydrate you, and the label warns about kidney problems linked to dehydration. Sipping fluids, small bland meals and protein when you can, and knowing when to call your prescriber. Plus a general 'ask your pharmacist which cold remedies suit you'. No product picks, no dosing, no skip-a-dose advice.

Then the likely contributors: eating much less, low fluids, low protein, poor sleep and dose-increase weeks, each flagged as a leading explanation, not a certainty. Practical fixes, and when tiredness means calling your prescriber. Builds on S1 10-31 without repeating it.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide constipation and fibre: why it happens (slower gut movement) and what helps (fluids, fibre built up gradually, movement)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 'Tirzepatide Constipation: What Actually Helps'. The first sentence names how common it was in the trials vs placebo (from the label). Explain the mechanism simply. Then a practical, food-first plan: build up fibre slowly, drink enough water, move, and know when to call your prescriber. Note that the advisory's 'avoid high-fibre foods in the first few days' advice is about nausea, so it doesn't conflict.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines after 65: are they safe with frailty? JAMA analysis (Oct 30), the SELECT frailty post hoc (semaglutide; fewer serious adverse events across frailty groups) and the Diabetes Obes Metab cardiovascular meta-analysis by age group (Oct 27)
candidates.angle: Body-worry 'honest uncertainty' Short: 'Semaglutide After 65: What the Frailty Data Show'. Use a semaglutide title because the SELECT evidence is semaglutide-only, and use 'GLP-1 medicines' for the class meta-analysis. What's reassuring (the SELECT post hoc) and what's still unknown (muscle, falls, fewer older adults in trials), plus why protein and strength training matter more with age. Label the SELECT finding post hoc.
candidates.why_now: A JAMA news analysis on Oct 30, plus a WorldHealth.net piece on falls after 65 (Oct 31). Medicare Bridge coverage is pulling older adults onto these drugs (Lilly said Medicare Zepbound demand beat expectations). Almost no creators cover the frailty question.
